items.stem:
Three judges ranked six entries in a science exhibition:
Judge I: 3, 5, 6, 1, 4, 2
Judge II: 4, 5, 6, 1, 3, 2
Judge III: 1, 5, 4, 2, 6, 3
Using rank correlation, find which pair of judges has the nearest approach to common judgement.
items.answer: Judges I and II (ρ = 33/35)
items.markingKey: ρ(I, II) = 33/35; ρ(I, III) = 3/5; ρ(II, III) = 11/35 (1 mark each); the largest ρ shows the closest agreement (1).

items.stem: The two regression coefficients are bᵧₓ = −0.1 and bₓᵧ = −0.9. Find the correlation coefficient.
items.markingKey: r² = bᵧₓ × bₓᵧ = 0.09; r = −√0.09 = −0.3 (r takes the common sign of the coefficients).

items.stem: If the correlation coefficient between X and Y is −0.5, find the correlation coefficient between U = 2X + 3 and V = 5Y − 5.
items.markingKey: r is unchanged by change of origin and scale except for sign; the scale factors 2 and 5 have the same signs, so r(U, V) = −0.5.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about correlation and scatter diagrams is correct?
items.answer: A scatter diagram gives a visual idea of the direction and closeness of a relationship.
items.markingKey: (a) Correct: "A scatter diagram gives a visual idea of the direction and closeness of a relationship." The other three are false.
options: A scatter diagram gives a visual idea of the direction and closeness of a relationship.
When both variables move in the same direction, the correlation is negative.
Correlation can be found from data on only one variable.

items.stem: Explain why ΣD must be zero when 7 items are ranked by two judges, and how this helps check your working.
items.answer: Both judges use the ranks 1 to 7, each summing to 28, so ΣD = Σ(R₁ − R₂) = 0; a non-zero ΣD shows an error in ranking or subtraction.
